name: Can the Fourier infrastructure be extended to handle polynomial progressions (Bergelson-Leibman)

knowledge.progressSummary: PROGRESS (Part XXV): EXACT spectral level-set distribution of the odd-modulus Weyl coefficient — #{r≠0:‖G(r)‖²=N·d}=φ(N/d) for each proper divisor d∣N (Finset.card_bij + Nat.totient_div_of_dvd), subsuming ALL prior moments (Parts XVII–XXIV) as its moments; punchline: maximal coefficient attained at EXACTLY minFac(N)−1 frequencies = exact major-arc count. 3 thm, 0 custom axioms, host-lean v4.26 clean.
insights: The existing Roth Fourier infrastructure is genuine and 0-axiom: RothTheorem.lean defines fourierCoeff A r = ∑_{x∈A} ψ(r·x) on ZMod N, proves Parseval (∑_r ‖Â(r)‖² = |A|·N), and the key linearization triple_count_fourier: tripleCount(A) + |A| = N⁻¹·∑_r Â(r)²·conj(Â(2r)). The 3-AP count linearizes ONLY because the pattern (x, x+d, x+2d) is a linear form: character orthogonality in x forces the frequency relation and collapses two of the three Fourier factors into Â(r) and Â(2r).

Structural answer to the OQ, part (a) — Sárközy/single square difference IS an accessible extension. For A ⊆ ZMod N the square-difference count SD(A) = ∑_{x,n} 1_A(x)·1_A(x+n²) Fourier-expands (identical orthogonality bookkeeping to triple_count_fourier) to SD(A) = N⁻¹·∑_r |Â(r)|²·G(r), where G(r) = ∑_{n∈ZMod N} ψ(r·n²) is a quadratic GAUSS sum. Principal term r=0: G(0)=N, Â(0)=|A| ⇒ |A|². The new ingredient vs 3-APs is that the non-principal terms are weighted by G(r) (size ≈ √N for r≠0 by classical Gauss-sum bounds) instead of a second coefficient Â(2r). So the LINEAR transform + Weyl/Gauss-sum estimates suffice — this is exactly the circle-method route to Sárközy's theorem.

Structural answer, part (b) — genuine polynomial PROGRESSIONS (Bergelson-Leibman) are NOT linear-Fourier accessible. Patterns with ≥2 nonlinear terms, e.g. {x, x+n, x+n²}, are provably NOT controlled by the U² (linear Fourier) norm: their count sees quadratic phase correlations invisible to Â. The required machinery is higher-order Fourier analysis (Gowers U^s norms, s≥3) plus PET (Polynomial Exhaustion Technique) induction, or the ergodic Bergelson-Leibman theorem via Furstenberg correspondence (see FurstenbergCorrespondence.lean). None of this — Gowers norms, inverse theorems, PET — exists in Mathlib 4.26. So 'extend the [linear] Fourier infrastructure' to the full Bergelson-Leibman setting is a >1000-line foundational program and open as a formalization target.

Depth-1 OQ chain (single -oq- segment) but 0 follow-up questions generated: the natural children (formalize the SD Fourier identity; formalize Gowers U³) are already captured as nextSteps here, and a new gallery OQ entry would just duplicate them.

Concrete first step on THE ONE REMAINING INPUT (the quadratic Gauss-sum magnitude): the WEYL-DIFFERENCING squared-magnitude identity |G(r)|²=N·∑_{h:2rh=0}ψ(−r h²) (sqGaussSum_mul_conj). Squaring G(r)=∑_n ψ(r n²) and reindexing m=n+h makes the phase r(n²−(n+h)²)=(−2rh)·n−r h² LINEAR in n, so the inner n-sum ∑_n ψ((−2rh)·n) collapses via char_orthogonality to N·[2rh=0]; only diagonal frequencies survive, weighted by the residual quadratic phase ψ(−r h²). This reduces the magnitude of a genuinely QUADRATIC exponential sum to a sum over the kernel {h:2rh=0}. Consequences: sqGaussSum_normSq_le (|G(r)|²≤N·#{h:2rh=0}, triangle ineq + ‖ψ‖=1) pins the sole remaining Sárközy quantity to the KERNEL COUNT (a gcd(2r,N) number), a structured replacement for the black-box √(2N); sqGaussSum_normSq_eq_of_kernel_trivial (|G(r)|²=N exactly, i.e. |G(r)|=√N, when the kernel is trivial — e.g. N odd & 2r a unit — the classical exact evaluation in the accessible regime). All 0-axiom, elaboration-clean.

Kernel-trivial discharge via unit frequency: IsUnit(2r) ⟹ (2rh=0→h=0) by left-mult by (2r)⁻¹ (Units.inv_mul), so ‖G(r)‖²=N exactly (sqGaussSum_normSq_eq_of_isUnit) and ‖G(r)‖=√N (sqGaussSum_norm_eq_sqrt_of_isUnit). For N odd, 2 is a unit (Nat.prime_two.coprime_iff_not_dvd + Nat.odd_iff → ZMod.isUnit_iff_coprime), so every unit frequency r gives ‖G(r)‖=√N (sqGaussSum_norm_eq_sqrt_of_odd). This is the concrete M=√N feeding sqDiffFree_density_bound on the unit/odd-modulus regime — replaces the abstract kernel hypothesis with a checkable unit condition.

The uniform bound off the 2-torsion (researcher, PR#38184): the Weyl kernel count gcd((2r).val,N) is a PROPER divisor of N exactly when 2r≠0 (since then 0<(2r).val<N), and a proper divisor of N is ≤N/2 (N=d·k with k≥2). Hence ‖G(r)‖²≤N·gcd≤N²/2 uniformly at every non-2-torsion frequency — the FIRST magnitude bound reaching non-unit frequencies (the exact √N results all required 2r a unit). For odd N the 2-torsion is {0} (2 a unit), so the bound is uniform over ALL r≠0, yielding an unconditional-in-N (composite included) odd Sárközy density statement with M=N/√2. The gap to a USEFUL bound: M=N/√2 is order N, not o(N); the √(N·gcd) triangle-inequality bound is lossy precisely when gcd is large (the surviving residual sum Σ_{h:2rh=0}ψ(−rh²) is itself a smaller Gauss sum with its own cancellation, discarded by norm_sum_le). Recovering the classical uniform √(2N) needs evaluating that residual sum (a recursion on the modulus), not just counting the kernel.

The two-torsion dichotomy G(r)∈{0,N} at 2r=0 is now fully decided: the N branch is UNREACHABLE for r≠0. Mechanism: at 2r=0 the n↦n+1 shift factors a constant phase ψ(r) out of every term (the mixed 2rn term vanishes), so G(r)=ψ(r)G(r); r≠0 gives ψ(r)≠1 hence G(r)=0. This is exactly the classical Σ_n(−1)^n=0 cancellation, but derived group-theoretically for the entire nonzero two-torsion at once, uniformly in N (no parity/N-mod-4 casework needed — the shift-by-1 argument sidesteps the N≡0 mod 4 obstruction that a shift-by-N/2 argument hits).

Two-torsion frequencies were the ONLY gap forcing Odd N in the density bound: at 2r=0 the gcd bound is vacuous (‖G‖≤N) but a nonzero two-torsion has G=0 exactly, so it clears N²/2 trivially — eliminating the last non-two-torsion vs two-torsion case split gives an unconditional (in N) uniform magnitude bound

Reverse kernel containment closes the last elementary gap in the shift method: the annihilator kernel {t:2rt=0} is EXACTLY the cyclic subgroup ⟨t₀⟩, t₀=N/gcd((2r).val,N). Proof is pure number theory — c·t=0 casts to N∣c.val·t.val; factoring c.val=g·a, N=g·b (g=gcd, Coprime a b) gives b∣a·t.val hence b∣t.val, so t=(t.val/b)·t₀. Consequence: the decidable canonical test r·t₀²≠0 is not just SUFFICIENT (Part XII) but detects EVERY shift-reachable vanishing — a shift making G(r)=0 via sqGaussSum_eq_zero_of_shift exists IFF r·t₀²≠0. Dually this EXACTLY isolates the residual frequencies r·t₀²=0 where no shift works and the residual quadratic Gauss sum S(r)=Σ_{h:2rh=0}ψ(−r h²) recursion is genuinely required for o(N).

Part XIV: In the residual case r·t₀²=0 (t₀=N/gcd((2r).val,N)) EVERY kernel element h=k·t₀ has r·h²=k²·(r·t₀²)=0, so every Weyl residual phase ψ(−r·h²)=1 and the residual sum collapses to the full kernel count g; hence ‖G(r)‖²=N·g is MAXIMAL and G(r)≠0. This is the exact converse of the shift criterion, closing the vanishing question to an iff.

Part XVI CLOSES the elementary o(N²) gcd-sum sub-goal from Part XV nextSteps: Σgcd((2r).val,N)=O(N^{3/2}) fully machine-checked, 0 custom axioms, NO Gauss-sum reciprocity needed — replaced the multiplicative-divisor-sum asymptotic plan with the sharper elementary d(N)≤2√N pairing.

HONEST scope: O(N^{3/2}) gcd bound gives Σ‖G‖²≤4N²√N (an explicit o(N³) second moment), but the resulting L²-averaged density in sqDiffFree_density_bound_l2 is NOT yet o(N) density — the RMS √(Σ‖G‖²)~N^{5/4} is too weak; sharp Sárközy still needs the exact second moment Σ‖G‖²=N·#{n²=m²}.

The prime-case √N algebra is not special to M=√N: for any sup-norm M≥0 the circle-method quadratic solves to |A|≤N(c+M)/(N+M). Extracting this decouples the ANALYTIC input (sharp sup-norm) from the ELEMENTARY solve-for-|A| step — a future sub-N sup-norm on any class of moduli now yields o(N) Sárközy with zero extra algebra.

Part XX: the exact second moment Σ_{r≠0}‖G(r)‖² is computable for EVERY odd modulus (not just primes) = N·(Pillai(N)−N). Primality was never needed — only that 2 is a unit (odd N), which trivializes the residual Weyl phase. Extends the Part XVII Θ(N²) cap on the L²-averaged circle method from primes to all odd N: second moment is exactly N·(Σ_{d∣N}dφ(N/d)−N), never o(N²).

The odd-N exact per-frequency magnitude ‖G(r)‖²=N·gcd((2r).val,N) upgrades every Part XV–XVI odd-N inequality (which lost constant factors via triangle/doubling bounds like gcd(2x,N)≤2gcd(x,N)) to an equality.

Part XXI extends the Part XVII prime-only L²-cap to EVERY odd modulus: the second moment Σ_{r≠0}‖G‖²=N·(P(N)−N) is bounded below by N·φ(N) since Pillai P(N)=Σ_{d|N}d·φ(N/d) always contains d=1 (→φ(N)) and d=N (→N), so P(N)−N≥φ(N). For odd N with boundedly many prime factors φ(N)=Θ(N), so the L² second moment is Θ(N²) and the L²-averaged density route is capped — the honest obstruction, now removed from primality.

The lower bound N·φ(N) is SHARP at odd primes: φ(p)=p−1 gives p·(p−1)=p²−p, coinciding exactly with the prime second moment sqGaussSum_normSq_sum_eq_of_prime (Part XVII). Equality P(N)−N=φ(N) holds precisely because a prime has only the two divisors 1,p.

Second moment tightly bracketed at every odd N: N·φ(N) ≤ Σ_{r≠0}‖G(r)‖² ≤ N²·(d(N)−1), both sides N^{2+o(1)} (Parts XXI+XXII). This CLOSES the order-of-magnitude question and reconfirms the L²-averaged circle-method route is Θ(N²)-capped; the crude explicit Part XVI upper bound ≤4N²⌊√N⌋ (N^2.5) is now superseded by the essentially-optimal N²·d(N).

Part XXIII: FIRST moment (L¹ Weyl norm) is subquadratic — (Σ_{r≠0}‖G(r)‖)²≤N³·(d(N)−1) so Σ‖G‖≤N·√(N·(d(N)−1))=N^{3/2+o(1)}=o(N²), STRICTLY below the Θ(N²) second moment. Cauchy-Schwarz (constant weight 1 over N−1 nonzero freqs) against Part XXII Σ‖G‖²≤N²(d(N)−1).

HONEST NEGATIVE (Part XXIII caveat): the o(N²) first moment does NOT break the small-minFac density obstruction. Parseval forces Σ_{r≠0}‖Â(r)‖²=|A|N−|A|², so the circle-method residual Σ‖Â‖²‖G‖ can only extract (max‖G‖)·Σ‖Â‖² (pointwise) or √(Σ‖Â‖⁴)·√(Σ‖G‖²) (L²) — never (o(N))·Σ‖G‖. The barrier is genuinely POINTWISE/minor-arc, not an averaging artifact.

Part XXIV: EXACT pointwise maximum of the Weyl coefficient at odd modulus — max_{r≠0}‖G(r)‖²=N·(N/minFac N)=N²/minFac N, ACHIEVED (IsGreatest), via ‖G(r)‖²=N·gcd((2r).val,N) + largest-proper-divisor=N/minFac. Upgrades the earlier minFac UPPER bound to an exact max; the sup-norm floor is exactly N/√minFac (closed form proven).

The full spectral DISTRIBUTION subsumes all earlier moments: value N·d occurs with multiplicity φ(N/d), so Σ_{d∣N,d<N}φ(N/d)=N−1 (all nonzero freqs) and N·Σ d·φ(N/d) recovers Part XX 2nd moment; distribution is the object the moments are moments of

Major/minor-arc separation is now EXACT for odd N: only minFac(N)−1 of the N−1 nonzero frequencies carry the Θ(N) maximal Gauss sum; the remaining N−minFac(N) frequencies sit at strictly smaller gcd levels — the honest structural input a refined circle method (past the proven single-frequency no-go) would isolate
